text: CORRECTED: the status below says "the walk test walks the crew's body over every leg of every candidate (208)"; it does not. The walk test (`walktest_navqa`, which runs Lot's `godot/addons/heist_nav_qa/nav_qa_director.gd`, last changed 2026-10-06 in Lot 0.97.2) walks a capsule of `AGENT_RADIUS * 0.7` -- 0.28 m at the bake's 0.4 m (:40, :818) -- on a floor of the bake slope plus one degree, 56 (:830), and nothing reads the contract's `walker_capsule_radius_m`. The crew's 0.35 m body walked once, over 18 kept walk tests on patched copies, 18 of 18 (`docs/findings/walktest_crew_body/`); whether the gate adopts it is item 208's open question. The cold run 9314 figures the status cites are not in the file it names. The class this item found -- a body the path query does not stand in for -- is so carried by 208, and the doors by 197 (Deli Counter 0.214.0, every walkable door to the contract's 1.25 m). The same sentence in `docs/findings/open_items_remeasure/README.md` is corrected there the same day (`docs/findings/narrowed_audit_2026-10-22/`).

the three preconditions stand where 2026-09-11 left them (Zoo `wallCorner.json` height 2.0-6.5 m with the 950-post measurement in its `dimensions_note`; `zoo_keeper/core/kit.py:116` `CORNER_ROLES = ("wallCorner",)`, mirrored at Deli Counter `themed_tscn.py:73`), and the promotion this item deferred has not been made: `deli_counter.py:1124-1135` seats every corner post with `size_mod="end"`, which `_slot_typename` (`:645-650`) names `wallEnd`, and `wallCorner` occurs in no Deli Counter source but the stem mirror, its test and a migration's docstring. What the promotion was waiting for -- corner art a post does not have -- now has its own home: item 79's facade planner asks for "corners as a designed condition rather than a remainder" and schedules it as `docs/proposals/FACADE_PLANNER.md` step 6, "the primary bay and the corners as designed conditions, after step 4's frames, with the walker", under the rule that any second layer of articulation is "subtractive or texture, never proud of the wall" -- so the designed corner may or may not want `wallCorner` at all, and that is step 6's to decide. Item 57's re-read of 2026-10-15 counts its own corner piece "shipped without a family" (item 58's post, ENV_CORNER_OPEN 988 -> 0). Two items point here and now point at 79's step 6: item 58's tier two ("see item 64") and item 74's close ("the `wallCorner` of item 64", one branch). Promoting before step 6 decides what a corner is would cost one exact module per (thickness, height) per building -- 17 across the library per theme and style -- and show nothing.

by item 84's decision, which answered this item's question: on a mesh with no interior vertices, wear does nothing in the engine. Level Factory 0.86.0's `zoo_worldskin.gd` draws COLOR_0 only on a GLB that is neither kit (`KIT_PREFIXES` wall_, wallEnd_, window_, doorway_, breach_, :35-36) nor tile (`TILED_PREFIXES` ceiling_, floor_, roof_ and `_dressing.glb`, :301-302) -- the branch at :956-968 -- and its comment (:1123-1130) cites this item's mechanism: 'Zoo computes wear per module, so on a module laid edge to edge it repeats per module by construction ... multiplied the 2 m module signature 3.8x'; item 84 CLOSED 2026-10-15, 'objects wear, tiles do not'. Zoo 1.120.1's `wear_colors` (`bpylayer/geometry.py:736`, `dark = min(1.0, concave * 1.5 + noise * 0.5) * wear`) still computes the term unchanged, so the finding stands in the file and cannot reach a frame. What this item said would close it -- occlusion as a property of the space -- is item 57's 'weathering in building space' (re-read 2026-10-15: not there), and the per-module repetition item 79's.

the texture leaves the GLB where the module is written and travels with it to the package. Zoo 1.2.0's `export_glb(..., share_textures=True)` (zoo/zoo_keeper/bpylayer/export.py:22, :72-73) rewrites every module's embedded images to `images[].uri` under `_tex/`, each named by a hash of its pixels and written once (zoo_keeper/core/gltf_textures.py:147-165, :215-222), so the detach runs in Zoo's export and not, as this item proposed, in Level Factory's. The folder travels: Level Factory 0.105.0's `scheduler._with_glb_dependencies` publishes whatever a collected GLB names beside it (level_factory/packages/jobs/scheduler.py:212-266, called at :716-719), Deli Counter's and Lot's copy sites carry it (`glb_deps.copy_with_deps`, deli_counter/portable_building.py:689 and :714, lot/lot.py:1986, lot/package.py:405), and the export refuses a package whose GLBs name a file it lacks (packages/exporting/export.py:2579-2599). In a package: cold run 9378's export.log line 17 reads 134 GLBs, 486 external references, 486 resolving to 209 files, 0 missing. What is left is not this item's: the duplication is now per building folder, not per module (9378's package: 451 `_tex/` PNGs, 112 distinct by sha256, one image stored 31 times), which item 28's closing status records and item 238 carries ('one per content per package is estimated at -10 to -12 MiB ... then the deduplication', NARROWED 2026-10-19).

the ruler this item asked for is in `shot_diff`: `tools/shot_diff.py` (55e1790, 2026-09-02, an hour after the status above) takes `--null` from a re-shoot of an unchanged run, refuses a null whose render provenance or subject does not match and asks `--null-of` when both runs photographed one subject (`:243-252`, `:265-360`), judges each shot's `max_d` against its own measured floor as `~floor`, `marginal` (within 1.5x) or `MOVED` (`:404-433`), and lists the shots inside the floor as 'no verdict' (`:449-454`); exercised on roadmap 214's weighted-normals A/B (`docs/findings/weighted_normals/level_shots_diff.txt`, 2026-10-09: 12 shots, floors 3-231, 8 MOVED, 3 inside the floor, 1 marginal), and item 92 builds on it. The null is opt-in: with `--images` and no `--null` the tool still calls any pixel over the threshold a move (`:403`) and does not say no floor was measured -- a guard worth adding, not this item's literal ask. The triplanar A/B was re-read against a null on 2026-08-29 (items 76 and 88: 7 of 8 shots clear their own floor, max |delta| 43-217 against 7-16; the 13.6-19.0 % reading survived, its quoted floor did not), and the 'survives triplanar' claims of 81, 84 and 86 rest on nothing open -- the outline was vertex normals, fixed in Zoo 0.52.0 and confirmed by eye (86), and 84 is CLOSED. What stands as this item's record: a pixel count needs a null; the frame mean does not at six frames and 1600x900 (zero to two decimals on eight shots) but is blind to a change that moves texels without moving brightness (item 87's retraction, 2026-09-05); and a floor belongs to one project, frame count and resolution.

both pieces left here belong to Lot's enemy placement, which the factory has since handed to a gameplay layer outside this pipeline: `docs/LEVEL_STANDARD.md:546-548`, "Spawns are provisional. The gameplay layer that will own them lives outside Level Factory, so a level-quality measure keys off geometry, not spawn placement"; item 132's reason for not fixing placement, a day after this status ("a real day's work invested in code that is leaving"); item 245 (CLOSED 2026-10-13), where Level Factory 0.202.0 shows Laser Tag's five fight verdicts and counts none of them in a pick; and item 241's record of INSTANT_CONTACT on all three of a run's candidates, "recorded, not tuned, enemy placement being provisional". The code stands where 2026-09-09 left it: `lot/site_spawns.py:556-569`, the distance branch's `clearance` still the crew's ground alone with its comment saying so, and `REACTION_SECONDS = 1.0` (`:107`), untouched by every Lot release since 0.53.0. If the gameplay layer never comes, both return as written here: two bodies' closing speed in the distance branch, and whether a one-second opening is what a brief wants. Found on the way: the docstring at `site_spawns.py:548-552` still says `lot.py` does not pass its solids to `place_enemies`; both call sites do (`lot.py:3041-3043`, `:3720`), as this item's body recorded -- a Lot text fix for the next Lot change.

THE PATH WAS REBUILT UNDER IT, two days after it was filed. The black rectangle was a single-sided emissive quad over opaque near-black glass; Pixelcoat 0.40.0 (781f5a0, 2026-09-13) made every theme's `glass` blend -- `glass_delco` at opacity 0.38 (`profiles/materials/glass_delco.json:15`) -- and refuses a theme whose glass would ship opaque (`see_through_fault`, `pixelcoat/core/material_grammar.py:946-969`, raised at `:1003-1005`), and Lux 0.36.0 (b5d498c, the same day) builds every window rig with no quad (`lux_light_loader.gd:1601-1616`, `show_emissive_quad = false`): what a window shows at night is the lit room through the glass. Seen from the street at night since: cold run 9132, 'the racks visible through the glass'; cold run 9120, 'the storefront through its glass'. The 0.32.2 double-sided quad (`runtime/rigs/lux_area_light_rig.gd:198-204`) remains for sign rigs the loader places (the fixture spawner turns it off under Zoo's sign hardware, `lux_fixture_spawner.gd:101-106`), and the night tint this item asked about was a question about an opaque skin that no longer ships on enterable windows; an Empty's opaque `glass_facade` is a different design and not this item.

THE WHITE BOX WAS REPLACED, NOT RE-TUNED, AND THE WALKER HAS READ A DOOR SIGN SINCE. The slab was a blank face: until Zoo 1.37.0 every derived door sign was 'a blank lit box' (102 in the library). 1.37.0 paints the face with the business's name at the pylon's emission 1.4 (`core/price_pylon_forms.py:91`), and 1.37.1 (4109dc1, 2026-09-30) builds it at albedo 0.15 and roughness 1.0 (`recipes/sign_box.py:18-19`), measured at a station square to a sign on cold run 9122's walk copy (a gas station's, not this item's hospital sign): pixels clipped to white 26.5% (control 26.4%) -> 20.0%, the field reading (78, 141, 110) and the rest the letters. The style row's 2.2 survives only on the pack path (`sign_box.py:91-96`), which Level Factory's fixtures job never reaches -- `adapters/zoo/__init__.py:321-341` passes no `--skins` -- and in cold run 9378's package all three door faces are painted at emissiveStrength 1.4. Read by the walker on the walk of 2026-10-14: 'double sign here looks...redundant', the band and the door both legibly reading DOC'S DISCOUNT DRUGS (Zoo 1.112.0); framed head-on by the factory's own shots in cold run 9218's `door_signs.png` (roadmap 220). The letters still clip at 1.4 'whatever the lamp does'; whether that matters is a look call, not this item.

the eye judged the drywall after this status, twice. The grammar: 0.28.0's read as a spotted hide on every interior wall and the walker called it, "We need to change/fix this", then chose its replacement from a second contact sheet, Pixelcoat 0.52.0 (305a124, 2026-09-27: fbm at 16 cells, blob share 9.2 %, ac1 0.64, held by tests/test_drywall_orangepeel.py and by `_SURFACE_NOT_NOISE` drywall ac1 >= 0.5, std 9-16, tests/test_theme_profiles.py; delco_1997 still maps drywall to drywall_orangepeel_delco, profiles/themes/delco_1997.json:17). In a level: the look review of 2026-10-19 showed a drywall partition from cold run 9335 (`r_wall_drywall`) under item 238's question, and the walker answered "Too soft or noisy" -- "you can tell where one texture stops and ends". Item 238 owns that answer and measures at that camera ("arms at the review's two cameras to name what the eye sees"), drywall's fine layer under BC1 among its named suspects (docs/findings/guides_2026-10-19/textures.md). Orange peel as relief stays unemitted (`"normal": false`). Pixelcoat 0.52.0 measured the limit: real orange peel is 2-5 mm against the pack's 7.8 mm texel, and "no grammar at this density can draw the finish the id names".

re-exported and measured. Cold run 9006 (begun 2026-09-11 20:31 on Level Factory 0.72.0, `docs/cold_runs/cold_9006/`) is the first package the fix exported, and item 17's record of its walk copy reads `texel_density` 537 kit surfaces, every skin 0.500 world-triplanar, worst mismatch 1.0x, its project.godot declaring the script and 49 of 49 sidecars binding it. Today's package keeps the shape: cold run 9376's `LF_restaurant_row_001.portable-godot` declares `[importer_defaults]` `import_script/path` `res://zoo_worldskin.gd` (project.godot:32-36), ships the script at that path, and binds it on all 39 of its kit-family GLB sidecars (`wall_`, `wallEnd_`, `window_`, `doorway_`, `breach_`), none empty. The code is `export.py:1224-1269` (`_worldskin_in_package`, `_importer_defaults_block`), pinned by `tests/unit/test_worldskin_declared.py`. The hand-patched 9005 copy this item named for a re-walk was retired for 9006's (item 17), and no walk since has reported a texel-scale jump at a remainder or an opening; the walker's "you can tell where one texture stops and ends" on interior walls (look review, 2026-10-19) is item 238's open question, whose planned arms include `tools/texel_density.gd`.

what this item found was a room-lighting fact, filed there the day it was measured ('FILED AS ITEM 147'), and 147 is CLOSED (2026-10-15: Deli Counter 0.206.0 lays a room's rows by its work plane; 957 of the library's 1,004 fluorescent rows off the centreline, 390 of 431 lit rooms with more than one run). The one piece the status above left -- `texel_density.gd` reporting a textured material with no UV set -- was planned against the refuted hypothesis and, as that status says, would have found nothing here; it is not built (`tools/texel_density.gd:79-104` reads only kit surfaces' `uv1_scale`), and `tools/glb_uv_census.py` already prints per GLB how many primitives carry `TEXCOORD_0` against how many there are (`:187`, `:236-242`), the count such a report would start from. Not re-walked: cold run 9005's ward, as 147 also records.

the stairs wear the building's floor family, and a themed package that draws any greybox is refused. Cold run 9061 refuted 0.72.1's concrete lookup: a card shop has no concrete wall, so 0 stair surfaces were skinned. Level Factory 0.93.0 (f906b9a, 2026-09-16) replaced it. `_skin_stairs` now dresses every visual `stair<n>_*` mesh from the first `floor_` kit module (`STAIR_FLIGHT_FAMILY`, assets/godot/zoo_worldskin.gd:93), and push_error()s when it cannot. Since 0.218.0 the export refuses any `gb_*` surface in a themed package (packages/exporting/greybox_skin.py:246-269; the census is a prefix test that names `gb_stair`). Cold run 9343 has apartment_walkup_a01 in its lot and exported "greybox skin: 0 surface(s) on a greybox material" (docs/cold_runs/cold_9343/export.log:16). Walked since, with no note on the treads: cold run 9070's package on 2026-09-23 (the stair note was the slab's cut collar, which item 168 owned and CLOSED) and cold runs 9305-9307 on 2026-10-14 (item 250). The `floor_hole` marking is items 265 and 250's (finding 6). The Zoo stair species built to Deli Counter's flights was this item's 'or, later'. The walker asked for it at the office's stair core (item 250, findings 7-9), and that ask is item 250's: 7 and 9 were met by Deli Counter 0.221.0 and 0.222.0, and 8's guard rail is still open there. Zoo still carries only `stair_rail`.

the walker passed the cars. The look review of 2026-10-19 asked "Do the parked cars read right?" over three frames: cars parked on a street and a row at the hospital, both in the inspection light, and a parking lot (`docs/findings/walker_review_2026-10-19/build_page.py`, section s44). The answer was "Looks right" (q44, `verdicts_2026-10-19.json`), with "some of the cars need some patina and wear...rusting....ect....bumper stickers....more lift". This was given on frames, not on a walk, and answers 'read right' rather than naming them as 1990s cars. Item 44 took the note up (Zoo 1.120.0 and 1.120.1, cold runs 9364-9366) and still carries it. Nothing jitters by the car's own measure: Zoo's coplanar matrix, re-measured on 2026-10-21 for 1.120.0 and again for 1.120.1, reads 646 builds and 0 same- or opposite-facing coincident pairs. The figure is recorded in zoo tests/test_car_forms.py:24-52, and the recipe's stand-offs are held above the probe's 2 mm window there (:256-268).

the open half was priced the day it was named, and what it found is a trade, not a task. Level Factory 0.101.0 (c28fae3, 2026-09-21, `tools/warmup_spacing_sweep.py`) swept the warm-up's station set on cold run 9066's package, with one cold and one warm launch per configuration, on an RTX 2060 on GL Compatibility. Cold load read 40.7 s at 9 stations, 45.3 s at 13, 48.6 s at 21, 49.0-51.2 s at 31-41 and 50.2 s at 79. So the ~48 s is the level's shader compile bill pulled forward, not the sweep's frames, and no station set removes it. Above ~16 stations lap 1's worst cold frame plateaus at 148-159 ms. The warm launch is the one that tunes, and `grid_spacing_m` ships at 40.0: 21 stations, 6.4-6.5 s warm load, 20.1-20.5 ms (`level_factory/assets/godot/warmup.gd:132`). Its measurements are in every package's `warmup.json`, cold run 9378's included. Left as a standing trade: a first launch on a cold driver cache pays the compile bill once per machine and driver, behind `warmup_finished`, where a host can show its own loading screen (warmup.gd:62-64). Every figure is one GPU's, and the magnitudes elsewhere wait for runtime data. Not re-priced since 9066: today's packages, with baked lights and sun and merged interiors, have not been measured for load.

the control sees its shadow, and what made it miss twice on 2026-10-10 is a standing unknown rather than a task. Every recorded run since has passed. The seven that night read the on-axis cap control at 0.001 against 0.459 unshadowed (`docs/findings/streetlight_shadow_control/`, `selftest_runs.txt`). Lux 0.77.0 records the test exiting 0 on 2026-10-14, windowed on GL Compatibility, on 0.76.1 and on 0.77.0 (`lux/CHANGELOG.md:76`). `shadow_gap_probe.gd` shows the control's own setting, a 5 mm cap at bias 0.03, blacks the pool (0.001), and `shadow_gap_probe2.gd` refutes a stale first read. The selftest is unchanged since Lux 0.65.0 (9237208), and a miss cannot pass quietly: the cap control is a counted `_check` (`tools/streetlight_shadow_selftest.gd:194`) and the test exits 1 (:205). If it fails again, keep the frame, the window's state (minimised, covered, the display asleep) and whatever else held the GPU. The selftest saves none of them itself: it reads the frame at :84 and prints.

the subject is fixed and proven twice, and what two runs of one command still disagree on is the engine's and the records'. The roof props: Zoo 1.109.0 (c2edb80) restarts every face `bevel_edges` leaves at its lowest vertex with its corner data (zoo/zoo_keeper/bpylayer/geometry.py:111-130, called at :406), and cold runs 9299 and 9300 built every one of the package's 596 GLBs and the lightmap to the same bytes (docs/cold_runs/cold_9300/NOTES.md:7-15). The applied scene's eleven energies: Lux 0.77.0 (4ce4c85) gives its three rigs `rest()` (lux/addons/lux/runtime/rigs/lux_fluorescent_rig.gd:50, lux_stage_light_rig.gd:58, lux_streetlight_rig.gd:156) and Level Factory 0.208.0 (b8fe4f7) rests every `lux_light_rig` before the pack (level_factory/assets/godot/run_lux_apply.gd:369-382); cold runs 9301 and 9302 read all 12 scenes Godot saves 0 lines apart once its per-save ids are masked (cold_9302/NOTES.md:13-14). Left, and not a task: Godot's own per-save ids (node unique_ids, drawn resource ids) and the metadata that records times, paths and the hashes of those -- 22 of 3,283 files, every one attributed, and read since as '247's residue, 0 lines once masked' (roadmap 20670). A package that must match byte for byte would need the ids normalised after every save; nothing asks for that today.

the walker judged the drawing, on 296's review page (`docs/findings/walker_review_2026-10-21_drawings/verdicts_2026-10-22/`, asked "Does this drawing read as the building?"): pharmacy_a01's, one storey, "Looks right"; deli_a03's and office's "Needs work" -- "we need to find a way to be simple and not noisy visually". Read: where a building has several storeys and many rooms, its furniture, room labels and dashed leaders crowd the structure the drawing exists to show. The simpler drawing is carried by 296, which asks what a player scopes out. LEFT here, as before: ramps, platforms and fire escapes in either drawing; a cut switchback's second leg drawn solid to its own storey.

the walker, on 296's drawings: "assume that in game, a player could rotate it", and what players should see is "simpler but carry all of the signals needed" (`docs/findings/walker_review_2026-10-21_drawings/verdicts_2026-10-22/`). A view a player turns is a model rather than one drawing, and this item's map mesh -- footprints, stairs, openings and holes kept; props, ceilings and tall walls left out -- is that shape; 296 points here for it. Not started.

the walker's answers on the review page, five of six (2026-10-22 12:11-12:15 UTC, `docs/findings/walker_review_2026-10-21_drawings/verdicts_2026-10-22/`, one document a question): "Does this drawing read as the building?" -- pharmacy_a01 "Looks right", deli_a03 and office "Needs work", deli_a03's note "we need to find a way to be simple and not noisy visually. assume that in game, a player could rotate it as well to"; "Should a facade carry a drawing?" -- "No drawing, as now"; "Is this the kind of drawing players should see?" -- "Simpler", "simpler but carry all of the signals needed"; "Anything a player should see that these leave out?" -- unanswered. The factory's half as this item framed it stands shipped and proven (below); the walker's verdict is that two of the three buildings cannot yet be scoped out from what ships. LEFT: a drawing simple enough to scout from that keeps every signal a player needs -- which signals is not yet written down (proposed, to put to the walker: each storey's walls, its doors and windows, its stairs, ladders and holes; furniture, room labels and leaders left out), with pharmacy_a01's density the bar; and a view a player can rotate, which is roadmap 295's map mesh. The in-game screen stays the game's.
